text.p: Philips Electronics NV said it had reached an agreement in principle with GC Capital, LLC on the sale of a plant in Greeneville, Tennessee.
The plant, currently operated by Philips Consumer Electronics Company, is used for manufacturing, warehousing and plastics moulding.
Philips said the sale was expected to be finalised in mid-December.
Philips said the Greeneville plant, which employs 1,800 people and makes over a million television sets a year, would remain important to its manufacturing plans under its new owner.
It said the streamlining of worldwide production, as reflected in the sale of the Greeneville plant, was aimed at improving Philips' performance and substantially reducing costs.
The Dutch multinational announced a major restructuring of its Sound and Vision division in July.
